name: Mary Bryant Home for the Blind & Visually Impaired

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a Certified FOOD Protection Manager (CFPM) who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

The PIC during this inspection was without a CFPM certificate available. When asked no-one else that was currently in the facility had the certification either. The PIC stated that someone that works in the facility was able to teach the class and he was planning on taking it for moving forward. Ensure that there are enough CFPMs available to cover all shifts in which foods are being handled/prepared.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.citation_text:
3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

Two cans were observed with significant dents in the storage rack in the dry storage room. The cans were shown to the PIC and education conducted. The cans were then moved for discard/credit during the inspection to correct. Ensure that all cans with significant dents are put aside so that they are not used and potential Botulism infections prevented.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
The back outside door has a gap in the bottom left corner allowing sunlight to pass through.  Gaps present in outside doors allow for easy entry of rodents and/or pests.  Ensure this gap is sealed to protect against rodent/pest entry.

6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Floor tiles in dish area were observed to be broken and separating from the floor.  Discussed with PIC, flooring shall be designed to be smooth and easily cleanable.  PIC stated new flooring is on the budget for this year and is actively looking to replace flooring.  Ensure flooring is smooth and easily cleanable to prevent accumulation of food and dust debris.

Multiple areas are in need of caulking to prevent accumulation of food, moisture and soil debris:
-Holes in wall in dish area.
-2 and 3 part sinks.
-Hand washing sink.
Ensure these areas are caulked to create smooth, non-absorbent, and easily cleanable surfaces.

6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
Allergen certifications for all CFM’s are expired.  Inspector commented on expired certifications during last routine inspection, although was not followed up on during spot checks.  Ensure all CFM’s complete allergen awareness training by next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Sanitation buckets were observed to have a concentration of 0ppm (quat) upon inspection.  Employee refilled buckets, showing a concentration of 100ppm.  Discussed with PIC and employee, kitchen manager will be advised of sanitation concentration in order to correct.  Ensure sanitizer dispenser is producing the necessary concentration level of 150-400ppm as according to label recommendation.

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Temperature measuring device is not available at the facility.  Discussed with PIC, temperature measuring device is required to read water temperature for sanitizing dishes.  Digital display on outside of the dish machine is not the temperature of the water as it sanitizes dishes.  Ensure a temperature measuring device is on-site and dish machine temperature is routinely checked for proper sanitation. 

4-302.13: (A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. (B) In hot water mechanical WAREWASHING operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the UTENSIL surface temperature.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Ceiling tiles and vents on kitchen ceiling were observed to contain dust and mold accumulation.  Discussed with employee and PIC, non-food contact surfaces shall be routinely cleaned to prevent contamination of food and equipment.  Ensure tiles and vents are regularly cleaned to prevent accumulation of dust and mold.

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
